layers.description: Geologic Map Schema (GeMS) version of the State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC) geodatabase of the conterminous United States.
layers.citation: Horton, J.D., 2026, Geologic Map Schema (GeMS) version of the State Geologic Map Compilation (SGMC) geodatabase of the conterminous United States: U.S. Geological Survey data release, https://doi.org/10.5066/P1A3DQZK.

columns.name: OBJECTID
columns.description: Object identification: an Esri default field that contains an integer value to uniquely identify a row in an attribute table.. sequential integer values. Source: Esri

columns.name: STATE
columns.description: State abbreviation. Source: US Postal Service

columns.name: MapUnit
columns.description: Short plain-text identifier of the map unit generated by combining the State, SGMC_Label and Prov_No fields. It is the linking field (key field) between other tables in the database. This field was previously 'UNIT_LINK' in the original version of the SGMC.. Values are unique within this database. Examples of values: "ALat;7" or "TXQhg;0". Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020; USGS authors

columns.name: IdentityConfidence
columns.description: Confidence that feature is correctly identified.. Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: Label
columns.description: Plain-text equivalent of the desired annotation for a feature.. K for Klippe and W for Window. Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: Symbol
columns.description: Reference to an area-fill symbol that is used on the map graphic to denote the feature.. Example of values: Custom symbol with the same value as Type.. Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: DataSourceID
columns.description: Source of data; alpha-numeric value used to link to DataSources table (foreign key).. Values are unique within this database. Example of values: "AL001". Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: Notes
columns.description: Additional information specific to a particular feature or table entry.. Free text. Values of <null> or #null indicate no entry.. Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: UNIT_NAME
columns.description: Name of map unit, copied from the FullName field of the DescriptionOfMapUnits table.. Examples of values: "Beaverdam Amphibolite" or "Alluvial deposits". Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020

columns.name: AGE_MIN
columns.description: Minimum age of unit copied from the CMIN_AGE field of the Age table.. Example of values: "Phanerozoic - Paleozoic - Cambrian". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: AGE_MAX
columns.description: Maximum age of unit copied from the CMAX_AGE field of the Age table.. Example of values: "Phanerozoic - Cenozoic - Tertiary-Paleogene - Oligocene". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MAJOR1
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a major component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Major1 thru Major3 only indicate that the lithology is considered a major portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Major1 is not considered more major than Major2 or Major3. All the Major fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of available entries.. Examples of values: "Limestone" or "Rhyolite". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MAJOR2
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a major component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Major1 thru Major3 only indicate that the lithology is considered a major portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Major1 is not considered more major than Major2 or Major3. All the Major fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of available entries.. Examples of values: "Basaltic-andesite" or "Shale". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MAJOR3
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a major component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Major1 thru Major3 only indicate that the lithology is considered a major portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Major1 is not considered more major than Major2 or Major3. All the Major fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of available entries.. Examples of values: "Dolostone" or "Volcanic". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MINOR1
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a minor component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Minor1 thru Minor5 only indicate that the lithology is considered a minor portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Minor1 is not considered more minor than Minor2-5. All the Minor fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Mudstone" or "Plutonic". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MINOR2
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a minor component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Minor1 thru Minor5 only indicate that the lithology is considered a minor portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Minor1 is not considered more minor than Minor2-5. All the Minor fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Siltstone" or "Metasedimentary". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MINOR3
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a minor component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Minor1 thru Minor5 only indicate that the lithology is considered a minor portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Minor1 is not considered more minor than Minor2-5. All the Minor fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Schist" or "Clay". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MINOR4
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a minor component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Minor1 thru Minor5 only indicate that the lithology is considered a minor portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Minor1 is not considered more minor than Minor2-5. All the Minor fields are considered volumetrically equal. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Basalt" or "Gypsum". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MINOR5
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as a minor component of the geologic unit. Copied from the Lithology table. Note that the fields Minor1 thru Minor5 only indicate that the lithology is considered a minor portion of the entire geologic unit as determined by the SGMC compiler. Minor1 is not considered more minor than Minor2-5. All the Minor fields are considered volumetrically equal. When units have more than 4 lithologies ranked as minor, they are concatenated in this field. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Anhydrite" or "Siltstone, Sandstone, Conglomerate". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: INCIDENTAL
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as an incidental component of the geologic unit. This field concatenates all incidental-ranked lithologies. Copied from the Lithology table. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Slate, Marble, Phyllite, Conglomerate, Mafic-volcanic, Limestone" or "Volcanic, Coal, Bentonite". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: INDETERMINATE
columns.description: Any lithology ranked by the SGMC compiler as an indeterminate (information does not allow ranking) component of the geologic unit. This field concatenates all indeterminate-ranked lithologies. Copied from the Lithology table. See appendix 4 of the data series report (Horton and others, 2017) for the complete list of all available entries.. Examples of values: "Shale, Siltstone, Chert, Quartzite, Greenstone, Sandstone" or "Rhyolite, Metasandstone, Quartzite, Phyllite, Metasiltstone, Sandstone, Conglomerate". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: REFERENCE
columns.description: The full reference citation.. Example of values: "Szabo, M.W., Osborne, E.W., Copeland, C.W. Jr., and Neathery, T.L., 1988, Geologic Map of Alabama, Geological Survey of Alabama Special Map 220, scale 1:250,000.". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: DIGITAL_URL
columns.description: URL (Uniform Resource Locator) web link address from which the original digital data of the geologic map can be downloaded or viewed if available.. Example of values: "http://www2.gsa.state.al.us/gsa/gis_data.aspx". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: NGMDB1
columns.description: USGS National Geologic Map Database URL (Uniform Resource Locator) web link address from which the paper version of the geologic map can be viewed or ordered if available.. Example of values: "https://ngmdb.usgs.gov/Prodesc/proddesc_55859.htm". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: NGMDB2
columns.description: USGS National Geologic Map Database URL (Uniform Resource Locator) web link address from which the paper version of the geologic map can be viewed or ordered if available. Used when more than one geologic map has been used to compile the state-scale map.. Example of values: "https://ngmdb.usgs.gov/Prodesc/proddesc_71888.htm". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: NGMDB3
columns.description: USGS National Geologic Map Database URL (Uniform Resource Locator) web link address from which the paper version of the geologic map can be viewed or ordered if available. Used when more than two geologic maps have been used to compile the state-scale map.. Example of values: "https://ngmdb.usgs.gov/Prodesc/proddesc_10177.htm". Source: Horton and others, 2017

columns.name: MapUnitPolys_ID
columns.description: Unique alpha-numeric value assigned to each feature (primary key).. Values are unique within this database. Example of values: "MUP000001". Source: USGS NCGMP, 2020
